_comment: SP-064: the image pick's rubric, read by lib/pick.js (Jev), shaped like scripts/story-rubric.json's axes. One Score question per scored cell and axis; Jev answers a level 0-2, and the axis score is that + 1 (decimals kept, as US-038 keeps them). An axis's optional "check" is added to its question. Must-see clarity checks the items with their adjectives (ADR-0032): the gate checks names only, so a partly cut item, or one in the wrong state, gets the lowest clarity.

plausible.label: Plausible
levels: the scene makes little sense: no setting clues, or the action happens in an order that doesn't fit the story
the scene makes some sense: a few setting clues, or a mostly sensible order of action
the scene makes sense: clear setting clues such as a floor, a hand or a height, and a sensible order of action

vivid.label: Vivid
levels: a flat, distant or ordinary shot at eye level
a closer shot or a somewhat unusual camera angle
an extreme close-up or a strong camera angle

clarity.label: Must-see clarity
clarity.check: Check each must-see item with its adjectives: the item must be shown in the state its adjectives give (a bare cob, a nametag that reads "Venice"). The cell's must-see marks say only whether the item itself is visible, partly cut or hidden; they don't check its state.
levels: a must-see item is partly cut off by the edge of the picture, is not in the state its adjectives give (a cob that isn't bare yet, a nametag that doesn't read "Venice"), or is small and hard to make out
every must-see item is shown in full and in the state its adjectives give, but some are small or unclear
every must-see item is shown in full, in the state its adjectives give, large and clear
